question.text: Priya wants to send her daughter abroad for higher education. The current cost of the programme is Rs. 5,00,000. If education inflation is 10% per annum, what will be the cost of the programme 8 years from now?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the Future Value formula: FV = PV x (1 + r)^n = Rs. 5,00,000 x (1.10)^8 = Rs. 5,00,000 x 2.14359 = Rs. 10,71,794. This is the standard inflation-compounding/time-value-of-money calculation supported by the workbook. The Trap: Rs. 9,00,000 results from using simple interest (5,00,000 + 5,00,000 x 10% x 8) instead of compound interest. Candidates frequently confuse simple and compound interest in time-value problems. Note: Goal planning for education uses the same compounding formula the workbook applies to any future-value calculation; the inflation rate for the specific goal must be taken from the client's own context or quoted explicitly in the question.
